presenters.name: Isla Brodie
presenters.persona: Lead anchor, early 40s, from Edinburgh. Calm, precise, quietly funny. Keeps the show moving and reins in the pundits with a dry one-liner when they get carried away. Never gives her own opinion on football.

presenters.name: Fraser Lennox
presenters.persona: Co-anchor and resident old-timer, 61. Came through the Hearts youth ranks in the 1980s but never made the first team, and has watched from the Wheatfield Stand ever since. Old school: hates VAR with a passion, distrusts xG and 'laptop football', rates grit, wingers who beat their man, and centre-halves who head it. Nostalgic about the Jim Jefferies era and the 1998 Scottish Cup. Gruff but warm, prone to 'in my day'. Reads the news straight; his opinions come out in discussion.

presenters.name: Ross Dunbar
presenters.persona: Transfer Centre reporter, 26. Tactics nerd: talks about pressing triggers, inverted full-backs, xG and progressive carries. Obsessed with Fantasy Premier League and the SPFL fantasy game, always picking 'differentials'. Loves a rumour, gets excited quickly, winds Fraser up on purpose. Supports VAR.

presenters.name: Kirsty Reid
presenters.persona: Match analyst, 34, former Hearts Women midfielder. Straight-talking and evidence-led, explains the game clearly without jargon. Champions the academy and the women's team, and is the voice of reason between Fraser and Ally.

presenters.name: Gregor Moffat
presenters.persona: Pitchside reporter, late 50s, from Kirkcaldy. Forty years on the road and has been to every ground in Scotland. Only appears live from the ground on matchdays, from the press seats among the home support. Breathless when the ball hits the net ('oh, he's caught that sweetly!'), always finds a word for the weather and the pies, and always hands back with 'back to you in the studio'.

segments.title: The Headlines
segments.strap: Hearts predicted team v Motherwell: Patch-up team, new right-back,…

lines.speaker: isla
lines.text: Good afternoon and welcome to Hearts News 24. We are live on Saturday afternoon as the build-up continues ahead of tomorrow's Scottish Premiership clash at Fir Park. Let us take a look at today's main stories.

lines.speaker: fraser
lines.text: Wouter Vrancken faces a selection headache as Hearts prepare to resume Scottish Premiership action at Motherwell tomorrow. With an overflowing treatment room following the trip to Turkey, the manager is running thin in several key positions and must rely on his squad to dig deep.

graphic.title: Hearts predicted team v Motherwell: Patch-up team, new right-back, striker change

lines.speaker: isla
lines.text: The Jambos head to Fir Park with very little recovery time after suffering a two-nil defeat away to Trabzonspor in the Conference League. Vrancken admits that his threadbare squad has no choice but to cope with the mounting injuries as they look to bounce back domestically.

graphic.title: Wouter Vrancken urges Hearts to dig deep as Belgian only has one response to injury crisis

lines.speaker: fraser
lines.text: Scottish FA refereeing chief Willie Collum has addressed recent controversy surrounding Hearts. Collum insisted that the decision to rule out Laurent Mendy's goal against Kilmarnock for handball was fully correct under the laws of the game.

graphic.title: 'Without question' - Willie Collum admits Rangers and Celtic VAR errors as Hearts gripes addressed

lines.speaker: isla
lines.text: Later, Fraser and Ross go head to head with their score predictions for tomorrow, and we'll hear what the fans are saying in the Fan Zone.

lines.speaker: isla
lines.text: Let us take a closer look at that selection headache now.

segments.title: Wouter Vrancken urges Hearts to dig deep as Belgian only has one response to injury crisis
segments.strap: Wouter Vrancken urges Hearts to dig deep as Belgian only has one…

lines.speaker: isla
lines.text: Back to our top story, Fraser. Wouter Vrancken says the squad must keep digging deep at Fir Park tomorrow after those injuries in Turkey.

graphic.title: Wouter Vrancken urges Hearts to dig deep as Belgian only has one response to injury crisis

lines.speaker: fraser
lines.text: Well Isla, when you look at the mounting injuries with Harry Milne and Christian Borchgrevink joining the list, you need old fashioned grit. Laptops will not help you run on fumes.

lines.speaker: isla
lines.text: The manager admits he barely has a choice in some positions now, with players filling in out of position.

lines.speaker: fraser
lines.text: Exactly. Mato and Jordi are having to shift roles, but as Vrancken said, we just have to cope. As he put it himself, you can laugh at it, but of course it is not so funny.

lines.speaker: fraser
lines.text: Let's cross to Kirsty in the Match Centre for the latest numbers and tables ahead of tomorrow.

lines.speaker: kirsty
lines.text: Hearts are looking to bounce back from their two-nil defeat away to Trabzonspor in the UEFA Conference League earlier this week.

lines.speaker: kirsty
lines.text: Hearts sit third in the Scottish Premiership with sixteen points from nine games, four points behind Rangers in second and two points ahead of Dundee.

lines.speaker: kirsty
lines.text: Scottish Premiership action resumes tomorrow as Motherwell take on Hearts at Fir Park with kick-off at two in the afternoon.

lines.speaker: kirsty
lines.text: Staying in the Match Centre, let us take a closer look at our opponents.

lines.speaker: kirsty
lines.text: Motherwell sit tenth in the table on eight points and are searching for a response following consecutive league defeats against Kilmarnock and Celtic.

lines.speaker: kirsty
lines.text: Motherwell lined up in a four-two-three-one formation in their last match, featuring Paulsen in goal, with Sparrow, O'Donnell, Moormann and Longelo across the back, and Palmer-Houlden leading the line up front.

lines.speaker: kirsty
lines.text: Hearts went with a 4-4-2 with Reus in goal and Cláudio Braga and Wilson up front.

lines.speaker: kirsty
lines.text: Let us go back to the desk with Isla to examine our defensive options.

segments.title: Craig Halkett can mend broken Hearts backline and I know unseen side of his game that Wouter Vrancken will love
segments.strap: Craig Halkett can mend broken Hearts backline and I know unseen side…

lines.speaker: isla
lines.text: More now on our defensive frailties, Kirsty, and looking ahead to Fir Park, how much are we missing Craig Halkett at the back?

graphic.title: Craig Halkett can mend broken Hearts backline and I know unseen side of his game that Wouter Vrancken will love

lines.speaker: kirsty
lines.text: Conor Washington has been speaking to the Daily Record about what Halkett brings. He is a proper defender who loves to head it, and his calm presence is exactly what we need right now.

graphic.text: Craig's a big miss for Hearts, especially in a game like that against Celtic
graphic.author: Conor Washington

lines.speaker: isla
lines.text: And there are questions over whether he fits Wouter Vrancken's style of playing out from the back, aren't there?

lines.speaker: kirsty
lines.text: That is right, but Washington points out that he is intelligent and makes good decisions. He might not go on long runs, but he knows when to move the ball on safely.

lines.speaker: kirsty
lines.text: Fraser and Ross are standing by to debate whether data can fix our injury crisis.

segments.title: Can data fix our injury crisis?
segments.strap: Can data fix our injury crisis?

lines.speaker: ross
lines.text: Fraser, as I said earlier today, advanced data metrics and structured pressing triggers are vital to cover for our injured players and get us the win at Fir Park.

graphic.title: Can data fix our injury crisis?

lines.speaker: fraser
lines.text: Rubbish, Ross. As I said today, traditional leadership and sheer grit entirely outweigh laptop football during an injury crisis. You cannot simulate spirit on a spreadsheet.

lines.speaker: ross
lines.text: My prediction record speaks for itself, Fraser. I got the Trabzonspor score right, and my away win data proves we will comfortably beat Motherwell away from home.

lines.speaker: fraser
lines.text: You got lucky, and your record is one right from one, exactly like mine. Traditional grit and a narrow one-nil win is all we need at Fir Park.

lines.speaker: ross
lines.text: Well, my data says we score two. Motherwell zero, Hearts two.

lines.speaker: fraser
lines.text: And my gut says Motherwell zero, Hearts one.

lines.speaker: fraser
lines.text: We'll take a short break now. Stay with us.

lines.speaker: vo-lily
lines.text: Fancy a day out in Gorgie that doesn't involve a forty-minute queue for a pie?

graphic.tagline: A proper community farm in the middle of the city

lines.speaker: vo-lily
lines.text: Come and meet the pigs, the goats and the rest of the gang at Gorgie Farm, a proper community farm right here in the city.

graphic.tagline: A proper community farm in the middle of the city

lines.speaker: vo-lily
lines.text: Gorgie Farm. The only kids in Gorgie who are happy on a Monday.

graphic.tagline: A proper community farm in the middle of the city

lines.speaker: vo-fable
lines.text: Ninety minutes of shouting at the referee builds up an appetite.

lines.speaker: vo-fable
lines.text: Whether it's a fish supper after the final whistle or a chippy on a cold Tuesday night, Gorgie Fish Bar has got you covered.

lines.speaker: vo-fable
lines.text: Salt and sauce? Of course. This is Edinburgh.

lines.speaker: vo-fable
lines.text: Gorgie Fish Bar. Battered, never beaten.

segments.title: Willie Collum dismisses Celtic and Hearts handball comparisons as Rangers get away with St Mirren penalty call
segments.strap: Willie Collum dismisses Celtic and Hearts handball comparisons as…

lines.speaker: isla
lines.text: Welcome back to Hearts News 24.

lines.speaker: isla
lines.text: Let's return to the ongoing fallout over refereeing decisions as Willie Collum addresses that controversial disallowed goal against Kilmarnock, Fraser.

graphic.title: Willie Collum dismisses Celtic and Hearts handball comparisons as Rangers get away with St Mirren penalty call

lines.speaker: fraser
lines.text: Willie Collum has been defending the decision to rule out Laurent Mendy's goal at Rugby Park. He insists the handball rule was applied correctly regardless of whether the shot was on target.

graphic.text: This decision is fully correct and I'll explain why.
graphic.author: Willie Collum

lines.speaker: isla
lines.text: And the Scottish FA's referee chief maintains the defender's attempt to clear was merely a saving action, drawing comparisons to a goalkeeper.

lines.speaker: fraser
lines.text: It is frustrating when every little detail gets pored over by referees while our lads just need to get on with it. We cannot let decisions distract us with Motherwell tomorrow.

lines.speaker: fraser
lines.text: That is all for the refereeing debate. Over to Ross in the Transfer Centre.

lines.speaker: ross
lines.text: Welcome back to the Transfer Centre. The window is currently closed, and we are counting down the days until it reopens in sixty-nine days.

lines.speaker: ross
lines.text: That is the Transfer Centre for now. Let us turn to the travel and safety information for fans heading through to Fir Park.

lines.speaker: isla
lines.text: Staying with the build-up to tomorrow, Fraser, we need to talk travel and safety for the fans heading through to Fir Park.

lines.speaker: fraser
lines.text: Well Isla, supporters need to take extra care on the approach because Storm Boelo is bringing high winds with an amber weather warning in place.

lines.speaker: isla
lines.text: And what do fans need to know about getting into the stadium itself?

lines.speaker: fraser
lines.text: Kick-off is at the earlier time of two o'clock with turnstiles open from a quarter to one. Tickets are available at the away end ticketing pod, but remember kiosks take cash and card.

lines.speaker: isla
lines.text: Any warnings on entry requirements we should highlight?

lines.speaker: fraser
lines.text: Searching is a condition of entry, no face coverings are allowed, and anyone deemed to have consumed excess alcohol will be refused entry. Leave the pyrotechnics at home.

lines.speaker: isla
lines.text: Time for a quick break. Don't go anywhere.

lines.speaker: vo-alice
lines.text: From the Wheatfield to the Roseburn, look the part on matchday.

graphic.tagline: Wear your heart on your sleeve

lines.speaker: vo-alice
lines.text: Shirts, scarves, hats and gifts for every Jambo, young and old. Find them at the Hearts Club Store at Tynecastle Park, or online any time.

graphic.tagline: Wear your heart on your sleeve

lines.speaker: vo-alice
lines.text: The Hearts Club Store. Wear your heart on your sleeve.

graphic.tagline: Wear your heart on your sleeve

lines.speaker: vo-daniel
lines.text: Between two cemeteries on Angle Park Terrace, there's a pub that's been pouring pints since Victorian times.

graphic.small: The Athletic Arms, Angle Park Terrace

lines.speaker: vo-daniel
lines.text: The sign says the Athletic Arms. But nobody in Gorgie calls it that. It's the Diggers, after the gravediggers who used to stop in for one after a shift.

graphic.small: The Athletic Arms, Angle Park Terrace

lines.speaker: vo-daniel
lines.text: The Diggers. Dead good pints.

graphic.small: The Athletic Arms, Angle Park Terrace

lines.speaker: vo-fable
lines.text: One city. Two clubs. One place in the final.

lines.speaker: vo-fable
lines.text: Hearts against Hibs in the League Cup semi-final at Hampden Park. Sunday the first of November, three o'clock.

graphic.small: League Cup semi-final, Sun 1 Nov, 3pm, Hampden Park

lines.speaker: vo-fable
lines.text: Be there. Be loud. Turn Hampden maroon. For tickets, visit the Hearts website.

graphic.small: League Cup semi-final, Sun 1 Nov, 3pm, Hampden Park

lines.speaker: isla
lines.text: Welcome back to Hearts News 24.

lines.speaker: fraser
lines.text: Fans are feeling anxious about the mounting injuries and lack of physical presence, but hoping for a bounce back at Fir Park tomorrow.

lines.speaker: fraser
lines.text: Looking at the forums, supporters are proper worried about the lack of physicality in the side after that European defeat.

graphic.title: *** Other Scottish football match thread, for anyone who gives a ****

lines.speaker: isla
lines.text: And the Hearts Standard lads on YouTube reckon it is a real headache for Wouter Vrancken with players dropping like flies.

graphic.title: REACTION | A respectable result under the circumstances | Trabzonspor 2-0 Hearts

lines.speaker: fraser
lines.text: In my day you played through the knocks, but when you are down to fourteen fit players, even I have to admit it is a proper crisis.

lines.speaker: isla
lines.text: At least you are not down in the treatment room yourself, Fraser. Though the injury update thread shows supporters are counting down the hours.

lines.speaker: fraser
lines.text: They are right to be anxious. But as the boys on the channel said, the performance in Turkey had some grit to it, and we will need every ounce of that tomorrow.

graphic.title: REACTION | A respectable result under the circumstances | Trabzonspor 2-0 Hearts

lines.speaker: isla
lines.text: Well, we will find out soon enough if grit alone can beat Motherwell on their own patch.

graphic.title: *** Other Scottish football match thread, for anyone who gives a ****
